tasks.title: Cladh Hallan Mummies
tasks.transcript: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Often when people think of mummies, we think of ancient Egypt. But mummies are found in many places. We recently studied a unique type of mummy in Scotland. Dating from the Bronze Age, about three or four thousand years ago, these Scottish mummies were found at a site called Cladh Hallan. This is the only place in Britain where prehistoric Bronze Age mummies have been found. Scotland's wet climate is not the kind of environment that usually preserves bodies well, so the discovery surprised researchers. The bodies had not been buried right away. Instead, they were deliberately preserved for hundreds of years before burial. Researchers also found that some of the remains were composite: parts from different people had been assembled. One clue to how preservation worked comes from bog butter. People in wet, peaty landscapes have long known that peat can keep organic material from breaking down, the same property that can preserve butter buried in a bog. The speaker mentions butter to show that prehistoric people in Scotland understood this property and used it. In that sense, the Cladh Hallan finds change how we think about prehistoric knowledge of the body and of the landscape.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: The differences between Egyptian and Scottish mummies
options.B: The discovery of prehistoric mummies in a surprising location
options.C: The process that gradually turns mummies into skeletons
options.D: The reasons that Bronze Age people practiced mummification

questions.analysis: 重点是苏格兰出人意料地发现青铜时代木乃伊。
